notes_list.title: Carbonyl One-Liners
notes_list.basic_overview: Aldol → beta-hydroxy carbonyl/alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl; Cannizzaro → alcohol + carboxylate from non-enolizable aldehyde; Wittig → alkene; Grignard → alcohol; Clemmensen/Wolff–Kishner → hydrocarbon.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Remember the product signature rather than only the reagent. Carbonyl → alkene strongly suggests Wittig or related olefination; carbonyl → CH2 strongly suggests Clemmensen or Wolff–Kishner; carbonyl + RMgX → alcohol after work-up.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Aldol → beta-hydroxy carbonyl/alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl; Cannizzaro → alcohol + carboxylate from non-enolizable aldehyde; Wittig → alkene; Grignard → alcohol; Clemmensen/Wolff–Kishner → hydrocarbon. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
